facts.statement: Wanosuchus is an extinct genus of sebecosuchian mesoeucrocodylian.
facts.quote: Wanosuchus ("Wangjiang County crocodile") is an extinct genus of sebecosuchian mesoeucrocodylian

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Wanosuchus is a nearly complete lower jaw.
facts.quote: It is based on IVPP V 6262, a nearly complete lower jaw, which is also the only known specimen.

facts.statement: The lower jaw of Wanosuchus lacks an external mandibular fenestra and contains thirteen teeth.
facts.quote: The bone lacks an external mandibular fenestra and has thirteen teeth

facts.statement: The fourth and eleventh teeth are the longest in the jaw.
facts.quote: the longest of which are the fourth and eleventh

facts.statement: The fossil was collected between 1970 and 1972 by personnel from the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology.
facts.quote: It was collected between 1970 and 1972 by Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology (IVPP) personnel

facts.statement: Wanosuchus was named in 1981 by Zhang Fakui.
facts.quote: Wanosuchus was named in 1981 by Zhang Fakui of the IVPP

facts.statement: The type species is W. atresus, named for the missing external mandibular fenestra.
facts.quote: The type species is W. atresus, a reference to the absent fenestra

facts.statement: Zhang classified Wanosuchus in its own family, Wanosuchidae, within the group Sebecosuchia.
facts.quote: Zhang classified Wanosuchus under its own family within Sebecosuchia, Wanosuchidae

facts.statement: Wanosuchus is known from Paleocene-age rocks in southern Anhui, China.
facts.quote: known from Paleocene-age rocks of southern Anhui, China

facts.statement: Wanosuchus lived from 66 to 56 million years ago during the Danian to Thanetian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Danian to Thanetian (66 to 56 million years ago)

facts.statement: Wanosuchus belongs to the parent group Eusuchia.
Wanosuchus shares some characteristics with the Late Cretaceous crocodyliform Doratodon.
facts.quote: It shares some characteristics with Doratodon, a crocodyliform from the Late Cretaceous of Europe
